t.E1202.agn: In 2020 EFSA concluded that, because of its chemical similarity to polyvinylpyrrolidone and the absence of adverse effects in repeated-dose studies, there was no need for a numerical acceptable daily intake (ADI) and no safety concern at the reported uses.
t.E1202.body: Polyvinylpolypyrrolidone is very poorly absorbed and most of it is excreted in faeces.
t.E1202.found.0: Food supplements in tablet and coated tablet form
t.E1202.prod: A polymer produced by polymerising N-vinyl-2-pyrrolidone.
t.E1202.regx.0: Re-evaluated; no numerical ADI needed, no safety concern at the reported uses.
t.E1202.regx.1: Its use as a carrier in egg-shell colouring tablets was added to Annex III.
t.E1202.summary: A synthetic polymer (PVPP). It is used to clarify beer and wine.
t.E1202.what: The water-insoluble, cross-linked form of polyvinylpyrrolidone; it is used as a colour and colloid stabiliser and as a clarifying agent.
